units.title: Differentiate a moving feature and scale the risk
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let H be a real inner-product normed space, with no completeness assumption. Let N be a positive natural number, lambda any real number, phi:R->H, and a,y,v in H. At a real time t assume the genuine derivative of phi is v. Then s↦||(a+phi(s))/N-y||² has derivative (2/N) inner((a+phi(t))/N-y,v) at t. Multiplying that risk by N/lambda gives derivative (2/lambda) times the same inner product. All divisions are real totalized divisions; lambda=0 is an algebraic zero-scaling case, not a temperature model.
assumptions: N>0; phi has actual scalar-parameter derivative v at t.
H is a real inner-product normed space; a and y are fixed arbitrary vectors; lambda is any real number.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual mean
steps.text: The derivative of N^{-1}(a+phi(s))-y is N^{-1}v; translations by fixed vectors contribute zero.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Differentiate the squared norm
steps.text: Apply the real Hilbert squared-norm chain rule to this residual, yielding its inner product with the derived derivative.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Cancel the genuine nonzero particle count
steps.text: Multiply by N/lambda and use N>0 to cancel N. This does not require lambda to be nonzero; totalized zero scaling remains valid.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

units.title: A literal finite-average risk equals its L² norm
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let P be any measure on a measurable space Omega, N any natural number, a_j:Omega->R for j:Fin N, and y:Omega->R. Suppose every a_j and y belongs to L²(P). Then the actual scalar squared residual (N^{-1} sum_j a_j-y)^2 is integrable, and its integral equals the squared L² norm of N^{-1} sum_j [a_j]-[y], where brackets are the equivalence classes of the stated functions. No probability or finite-measure hypothesis is needed. N=0 uses the empty sum and totalized real inverse.
assumptions: Every selected scalar feature a_j and the label function y is genuinely MemLp at exponent2 under P.
P is any measure; N may be zero in this finite-average identity.

steps.title: Produce the actual residual in L²
steps.text: Finite sums, scalar multiplication and subtraction preserve L² membership. Therefore its square is integrable.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Identify the representative
steps.text: Use the almost-everywhere representative identities for each actual toLp class, finite sum, scalar multiple and difference. The assembled class represents the actual scalar residual.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Evaluate the Hilbert norm
steps.text: The L² inner product is the actual integral of pointwise products, and the squared norm is the self inner product.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

units.title: Construct the empirical law and evaluate its actual risk
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let W be a measurable space with measurable singleton points, Omega a measurable data space and P any measure on Omega. Let N>0, w:Fin N->W, scalar features K:W->Omega->R, and a label y:Omega->R. Suppose K(w_j) and y are in L²(P). Define rho=N^{-1} sum_j Dirac(w_j), using reciprocal N as an ENNReal measure weight. Then rho is a probability measure, the actual loss (integral K(q,omega) drho(q)-y(omega))² is integrable under P, and its integral equals ||N^{-1} sum_j [K(w_j)]-[y]||². Particle values may coincide. No global measurability in q or probability assumption on P is required for this finite atomic assertion.
assumptions: N>0; W has measurable singleton points.
Every selected feature K(w_j) and y is in L²(P); repeated atoms are allowed.

steps.title: Normalize the actual finite measure
steps.text: The sum of N Dirac masses has total mass N. Its nonzero finite reciprocal weight gives total mass one.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Evaluate each actual predictor slice
steps.text: Every function is integrable under a Dirac at a measurable singleton point. Finite-measure-sum and scalar integration give the literal predictor for every data point.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Apply the finite residual identity
steps.text: The actual predictor is now the finite average, so the previous L² residual theorem yields both loss integrability and the exact risk norm.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

units.title: One indexed replacement has an exact quadratic remainder
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let H be any real inner-product normed space, N>0, a:Fin N->H, i:Fin N, and u,y in H. Let b be any real number and assume ||a_i||<=b and ||u||<=b. Define m=N^{-1} sum_j a_j and mNew=N^{-1} sum_j Function.update(a,i,u)_j. Then ||mNew-y||²-||m-y||²-2 inner(m-y,mNew-m)=||mNew-m||², and this squared remainder is at most4b²/N². The mean displacement is derived, not assumed. No bound on y or the other features, completeness, or measure hypothesis is needed.
assumptions: N>0; only the selected old feature and its replacement have norm at most b.
Repeated feature values are allowed; Function.update changes one index. The two norm bounds imply b>=0.

steps.title: Cancel exactly one index
steps.text: In the difference of the two finite sums all j≠i terms cancel, including terms whose vector values equal a_i.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Bound the actual displacement
steps.text: The triangle inequality and the two individual norm bounds give a bound on the derived displacement.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Expand the unhalved quadratic loss
steps.text: Write mNew-y=(m-y)+Delta and use the real inner-product norm expansion. The exact cross term has factor2.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Square the nonnegative norm bound
steps.text: Both norms and 2b/N are nonnegative; squaring produces the stated constant.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

units.title: Integrate the quadratic potential before taking the remainder
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let W be measurable and H a complete real inner-product space. Let mu and nu be arbitrary measures, feature:W->H Bochner integrable under each, and y in H. Put m=integral feature dmu, n=integral feature dnu and V(q)=2 inner(m-y,feature(q)). Then V is integrable under both measures. With D=integral V dnu-integral V dmu, one has D=2 inner(m-y,n-m), ||n-y||²-||m-y||²-D=||n-m||², and ||m-y||²+D<=||n-y||². The real function t↦||m+t(n-m)-y||² has derivative D at zero. No probability, finite-mass or equal-mass hypothesis is imposed: m and n are unnormalized integrals.
assumptions: H is complete; the H-valued feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under both measures.
The fixed label is any vector. The measures may have unequal or infinite total mass.

steps.title: Produce scalar potential integrability
steps.text: Pairing the actual feature with a fixed Hilbert vector is a continuous linear functional. It preserves Bochner integrability under either measure.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Commute each integral with the linear pairing
steps.text: Subtract the two actual finite scalar integrals and use linearity in the second inner-product argument. Here eta is restricted to mu or nu, precisely the two supplied integrability domains.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Expand the loss and use positivity
steps.text: Expand n-y=(m-y)+(n-m); the leftover squared norm is nonnegative and yields the support inequality.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Differentiate the literal affine Hilbert curve
steps.text: Its residual derivative is n-m. The squared-norm chain rule gives precisely D at zero.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

units.title: A true joint-data risk has a positive empirical replacement budget
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let W be measurable with measurable singleton points, X measurable, and P a probability measure on X×R with input marginal PX=P.map fst. Let K:W->X->R. Suppose each K(q) is genuinely in L²(PX), every corresponding L² norm is at most the same b>0, and the true response coordinate z↦z.2 is in L²(P). For any N>0, configuration w:Fin N->W, index i and replacement u, define rho=N^{-1} sum_j Dirac(w_j), rhoNew by replacing only index i, predictor_law(x)=integral K(q,x) dlaw(q), risk(law)=integral(predictor_law(z.1)-z.2)² dP(z), and V(q)=2 integral(predictor_rho(z.1)-z.2)K(q,z.1) dP(z). Put D=integral V drhoNew-integral V drho. Then4b²>0; both empirical laws are probabilities; both actual losses and both finite-law potential integrals are integrable; D=(V(u)-V(w_i))/N; and risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-D equals the input-marginal integral of (predictor_rhoNew-predictor_rho)². This remainder is nonnegative and at most4b²/N². No independence of input and response, global parameter measurability, or assumed pairing/remainder/displacement bound is used.
assumptions: P is the true joint data probability; PX is its pushforward by fst, and z.2 is the actual response.
For every q, K(q) is in L²(PX) with norm at most one common b>0; z.2 is in L²(P).
N>0; measurable singleton points permit actual finite Dirac integration. Repeated particle values are allowed.

steps.title: Construct and evaluate both empirical laws
steps.text: Normalize the actual N Dirac masses, and integrate each fixed scalar slice by the finite-sum identity. Updating the configuration changes exactly one index.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Lift through the true marginal
steps.text: Work in H=L²(P). Write a_q=[K(q) composed with fst], y=[z↦z.2], m=N^{-1} sum_j a_(w_j), and mNew=N^{-1} sum_j a_(updated w_j). The map fst preserves P to its actual pushforward PX. Its L² pullback is an isometry. Thus the actual lifted features have the supplied norm bound under the same joint P, and the actual residual is in L².
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Identify the actual potential
steps.text: Identify the actual finite predictor residual with its L² class. Integrating its product with each actual lifted feature gives the Hilbert inner product; both factors are in L².
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Produce the finite signed pairing
steps.text: Integrate this same potential under each actual empirical law. Finite-sum cancellation and linearity give both the indexed update and the mean-displacement pairing.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Identify the exact scalar remainder
steps.text: Apply the finite Hilbert replacement identity and identify both risk norms with their actual scalar losses. Push the squared predictor difference back to the true input marginal.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.

steps.title: Obtain the uniform positive budget
steps.text: The two actual lifted feature norms are at most b; their indexed average changes by at most2b/N. Square that derived estimate. The supplied positive b makes the shared budget coefficient strictly positive.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are extracted from the adjacent compiled module; the mathematical step is explained here.
